• Los ingresos por la producción de arenas bituminosas se disparan un 32 % hasta alcanzar los 9.32 mil millones de dólares canadienses en el trimestre
  • Tanto la producción en la fase de exploración y producción como el volumen de procesamiento de las refinerías disminuyeron en el tercer trimestre
  • Suncor aumentó la recompra mensual de acciones a 750 millones de dólares canadienses a partir de octubre

Se añaden detalles y contexto a lo largo del texto

3 nov (Reuters) - La productora integrada de petróleo y gas canadiense Suncor Energy SU.TO superó el martes las expectativas de los analistas en cuanto a beneficios del tercer trimestre, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo y la solidez de los márgenes de refino ayudaron a compensar la disminución de los volúmenes de producción y procesamiento.

La guerra de Irán (link), que ya entra en su noveno mes, ha perturbado el suministro energético mundial, lo que ha provocado un aumento de los precios del crudo. El precio medio del crudo de referencia Brent se situó en 89,27 dólares por barril durante el trimestre, un 31 % más que el año anterior.

Las empresas petroleras integradas, como Imperial Oil IMO.TO y Suncor, se han beneficiado de un mercado mundial de combustibles agitado por la guerra, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo ha reforzado los márgenes tanto en la producción como en el refinado.

La semana pasada, Imperial Oil IMO.TO también superó las previsiones de los analistas en cuanto a beneficios trimestrales, gracias a los sólidos márgenes de refino.

Durante el trimestre, Suncor registró una caída tanto en la producción en la fase inicial como en los volúmenes de procesamiento. Sin embargo, el aumento de los precios del petróleo contribuyó a que los ingresos procedentes de la producción de arenas bituminosas se incrementaran un 32 %, hasta alcanzar los 9.32 mil millones de dólares canadienses (6.66 mil millones de dólares).

Los ingresos procedentes de sus operaciones de refino se dispararon más del 65 %, hasta alcanzar unos 13 400 millones de dólares canadienses, impulsados por un aumento de más del doble en los márgenes de craqueo de referencia, lo que permitió a las refinerías obtener beneficios significativamente mayores por el procesamiento de cada barril de crudo.

La producción upstream de la empresa, con sede en Calgary (Alberta), cayó un 2 %, hasta los 852 500 barriles diarios, mientras que el volumen de procesamiento de las refinerías descendió ligeramente hasta los 487 700 bpd.

Suncor anunció un dividendo trimestral de 66 céntimos canadienses por acción, pagadero el 24 de diciembre, lo que supone un aumento del 10 % con respecto al trimestre anterior.

En octubre, Suncor acordó vender sus participaciones (link) en tres activos petroleros en alta mar de Canadá a Ithaca ITH.L por 1.200 millones de dólares canadienses y aumentó las recompras de acciones de 500 millones a 750 millones de dólares canadienses al mes a partir de octubre.

La empresa registró un beneficio operativo ajustado de 3,97 dólares canadienses por acción en el trimestre finalizado el 30 de septiembre, frente a la estimación media de los analistas de 3,28 dólares canadienses por acción, según datos recopilados por LSEG.

(1 dólar = 1,3998 dólares canadienses)

ACUERDOS

PRIMERO. Se autoriza, por esta única ocasión: (a) la transferencia de la totalidad de los recursos derivados de las ventas de los autobuses que formaban parte del patrimonio del Fideicomiso de Garantía y que fueron vendidos por la Fideicomitente durante los ejercicios 2025 y 2026, mismos que actualmente se encuentran depositados en la Cuenta de Ingresos del Fideicomiso, como se indica a continuación: (i) $10,624,728.10 (diez millones seiscientos veinticuatro mil setecientos veintiocho Pesos 10/100) al Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda, y (ii) el restante a la cuenta del Fondo Capex del Fideicomiso; en el entendido que (i) dichos recursos deberán permanecer reservados en la cuenta del Fondo Capex y/o en el Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda, según corresponda, mismos que serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C (incluyendo el pago de intereses de los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses por lo que respecta a las cantidades que se transfieran al Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda), lo anterior salvo por el pago de principal pagadero bajo los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses existentes y revelados a la fecha de la presente Asamblea, con cargo al Fondo Capex, hasta la fecha en que cada uno de dichos Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses sean liquidados en su totalidad. Todo lo anterior, sujeto a la condición suspensiva consistente en que la Fideicomitente aporte todos los Autobuses relacionados con los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses correspondientes, al Fideicomiso de Garantía, cuya aportación estará a su vez, sujeta a la condición de que se liquide en su totalidad el Financiamiento para la Adquisición de Autobuses correspondiente y, en consecuencia, se libere la garantía de la armadora correspondiente. Para efectos de lo anterior, se instruye al Fiduciario a liberar los recursos necesarios del Fondo Capex para pagar dichos Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses, mes a mes, conforme los pagos sean exigibles bajo dichos financiamientos, sin que sean necesarias autorizaciones de presupuesto adicionales. La Asamblea y los Tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en relación con las ventas de autobuses realizadas sin las autorizaciones correspondientes, así como en caso de cualquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (b) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior.

SEGUNDO. Se autoriza, por esta única ocasión: (a) la liberación de los recursos correspondientes al Presupuesto de Capex aprobado para el ejercicio 2025, por un monto de hasta $36,878,325.31 (treinta y seis millones, ochocientos setenta y ocho mil trescientos veinticinco Pesos 31/100), y su aplicación al pago de los conceptos correspondientes, únicamente por lo que respecta al mes de noviembre de 2026, incluyendo sin limitar, al pago de Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses; en el entendido que, todos los recursos autorizados conforme al presente Acuerdo serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C, lo anterior, salvo por el pago de los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobses, de acuerdo con lo establecido en este Acuerdo, en el entendido, además, que cualquier uso de los recursos para fines distintos de los establecidos en los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C será considerado un incumplimiento a la Cláusula Séptima (Destino Específico de los Fondos) del Fideicomiso para todos los efectos legales a que haya lugar, así como a las demás obligaciones que resulten aplicables y, por lo tanto, constituirá un Evento de Incumplimiento; en el entendido, además, que la autorización contenida en el presente Acuerdo no constituye ni deberá interpretarse como una dispensa, renuncia o modificación a cualquier derecho u obligación

conforme a los Documentos de Emisión, ni como un precedente para autorizaciones futuras, por lo que no se otorgan dispensas de ninguna naturaleza. Asimismo, la Asamblea y los Tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en caso de cualquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (b) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior.

TERCERO. Se autoriza la contratación de KPMG Cárdenas Dosal, S.C. como el despacho de contadores públicos encargado de realizar la auditoría externa del Fideicomiso para el ejercicio 2026, en los términos de la propuesta de servicios que fue presentada a la Asamblea, y en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, al Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contrato y/o convenio, en relación con lo anterior.

CUARTO. Se toma conocimiento del informe presentado por parte del Asesor Especializado, respecto de los presupuestos presentados por la Fideicomitente correspondientes al mes de noviembre de 2026, y, en consecuencia, se aprueba: (a) el presupuesto de Gastos de Mantenimiento de la Emisión, el presupuesto de Gastos de Prestadores de Servicios, el presupuesto de Gastos Adicionales y el presupuesto de Gastos Generales, todo lo anterior aplicable al mes de noviembre de 2026, tomando como referencia la propuesta presentada por la Fideicomitente y considerando los ajustes presentados por el Asesor Especializado, mismos que cuentan con la validación del Supervisor de Mantenimiento, (b) el Programa de Renovación de Autobuses para 2026 presentado por la Fideicomitente para el mes de noviembre de 2026, únicamente por lo que respecta a la venta de autobuses, en el entendido que, de llevarse a cabo la venta de autobuses conforme al Programa de Renovación de Autobuses aprobado, el producto de cualesquier venta que se obtenga, deberá depositarse y reservarse en la cuenta del Fondo Capex del Fideicomiso, hasta que una asamblea de Tenedores posterior apruebe el Presupuesto de Capex; en el entendido, además, que todos los recursos autorizados conforme al presente Acuerdo, serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documento de Emisión y la hoja de términos y condiciones de fecha 3 de abril de 2025 (la "Hoja de T&C"). Cualquier uso de los recursos para fines distintos de los establecidos en los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C, será considerado un incumplimiento a la Cláusula Séptima (Destino Específico de los Fondos) del Fideicomiso para todos los efectos legales a que haya lugar, así como a las demás obligaciones que resulten aplicables y, por lo tanto, constituirá un Evento de Incumplimiento. Asimismo, la Asamblea y los tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en caso de cualesquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (c) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior, en el entendido que la presente autorización, no constituye una dispensa a cualquier Eventos de Incumplimiento, ni la las consecuencias derivadas de los mismos.

QUINTO. Se autoriza, por esta única ocasión: (a) la transferencia de la totalidad de los recursos derivados de las ventas de los autobuses que formaban parte del patrimonio del Fideicomiso de Garantía y que fueron vendidos por la Fideicomitente durante los ejercicios 2025 y 2026, mismos que actualmente se encuentran depositados en la Cuenta de Ingresos del Fideicomiso, como se indica a continuación: (i) $10,624,728.10 (diez millones seiscientos veinticuatro mil setecientos veintiocho Pesos 10/100) al Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda, y (ii) el restante a la cuenta del Fondo Capex del Fideicomiso; en el entendido que (i) dichos recursos deberán permanecer reservados en la cuenta del Fondo Capex y/o en el Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda, según corresponda, mismos que serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C (incluyendo el pago de intereses de los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses por lo que respecta a las cantidades que se transfieran al Fondo de Reserva del Servicio de Deuda), lo anterior salvo por el pago de principal pagadero bajo los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses existentes y revelados a la fecha de la presente Asamblea, con cargo al Fondo Capex, hasta la fecha en que cada uno de dichos Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses sean liquidados en su totalidad. Todo lo anterior, sujeto a la condición suspensiva consistente en que la Fideicomitente aporte todos los Autobuses relacionados con los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses correspondientes, al Fideicomiso de Garantía, cuya aportación estará a su vez, sujeta a la condición de que se liquide en su totalidad el Financiamiento para la Adquisición de Autobuses correspondiente y, en consecuencia, se libere la garantía de la armadora correspondiente. Para efectos de lo anterior, se instruye al Fiduciario a liberar los recursos necesarios del Fondo Capex para pagar dichos Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses, mes a mes, conforme los pagos sean exigibles bajo dichos financiamientos, sin que sean necesarias autorizaciones de presupuesto adicionales. La Asamblea y los Tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en relación con las ventas de autobuses realizadas sin las autorizaciones correspondientes, así como en caso de cualquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (b) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior.

SEGUNDO. Se autoriza, por esta única ocasión: (a) la liberación de los recursos correspondientes al Presupuesto de Capex aprobado para el ejercicio 2025, por un monto de hasta $36,878,325.31 (treinta y seis millones, ochocientos setenta y ocho mil trescientos veinticinco Pesos 31/100), y su aplicación al pago de los conceptos correspondientes, únicamente por lo que respecta al mes de noviembre de 2026, incluyendo sin limitar, al pago de Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobuses; en el entendido que, todos los recursos autorizados conforme al presente Acuerdo serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C, lo anterior, salvo por el pago de los Financiamientos para la Adquisición de Autobses, de acuerdo con lo establecido en este Acuerdo, en el entendido, además, que cualquier uso de los recursos para fines distintos de los establecidos en los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C será considerado un incumplimiento a la Cláusula Séptima (Destino Específico de los Fondos) del Fideicomiso para todos los efectos legales a que haya lugar, así como a las demás obligaciones que resulten aplicables y, por lo tanto, constituirá un Evento de Incumplimiento; en el entendido, además, que la autorización contenida en el presente Acuerdo no constituye ni deberá interpretarse como una dispensa, renuncia o modificación a cualquier derecho u obligación

conforme a los Documentos de Emisión, ni como un precedente para autorizaciones futuras, por lo que no se otorgan dispensas de ninguna naturaleza. Asimismo, la Asamblea y los Tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en caso de cualquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (b) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior.

TERCERO. Se autoriza la contratación de KPMG Cárdenas Dosal, S.C. como el despacho de contadores públicos encargado de realizar la auditoría externa del Fideicomiso para el ejercicio 2026, en los términos de la propuesta de servicios que fue presentada a la Asamblea, y en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, al Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contrato y/o convenio, en relación con lo anterior.

CUARTO. Se toma conocimiento del informe presentado por parte del Asesor Especializado, respecto de los presupuestos presentados por la Fideicomitente correspondientes al mes de noviembre de 2026, y, en consecuencia, se aprueba: (a) el presupuesto de Gastos de Mantenimiento de la Emisión, el presupuesto de Gastos de Prestadores de Servicios, el presupuesto de Gastos Adicionales y el presupuesto de Gastos Generales, todo lo anterior aplicable al mes de noviembre de 2026, tomando como referencia la propuesta presentada por la Fideicomitente y considerando los ajustes presentados por el Asesor Especializado, mismos que cuentan con la validación del Supervisor de Mantenimiento, (b) el Programa de Renovación de Autobuses para 2026 presentado por la Fideicomitente para el mes de noviembre de 2026, únicamente por lo que respecta a la venta de autobuses, en el entendido que, de llevarse a cabo la venta de autobuses conforme al Programa de Renovación de Autobuses aprobado, el producto de cualesquier venta que se obtenga, deberá depositarse y reservarse en la cuenta del Fondo Capex del Fideicomiso, hasta que una asamblea de Tenedores posterior apruebe el Presupuesto de Capex; en el entendido, además, que todos los recursos autorizados conforme al presente Acuerdo, serán destinados única y exclusivamente a los fines específicos que establecen los Documento de Emisión y la hoja de términos y condiciones de fecha 3 de abril de 2025 (la "Hoja de T&C"). Cualquier uso de los recursos para fines distintos de los establecidos en los Documentos de Emisión y la Hoja de T&C, será considerado un incumplimiento a la Cláusula Séptima (Destino Específico de los Fondos) del Fideicomiso para todos los efectos legales a que haya lugar, así como a las demás obligaciones que resulten aplicables y, por lo tanto, constituirá un Evento de Incumplimiento. Asimismo, la Asamblea y los tenedores se reservan todos los derechos que les correspondan conforme a los Documentos de Emisión y la ley aplicable en caso de cualesquier incumplimiento a las disposiciones establecidas en el presente Acuerdo; y (c) llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios en relación con todo lo anterior y, en consecuencia, se autoriza e instruye al Fiduciario, a la Fideicomitente, al Representante Común y a los miembros del Comité Técnico designados por este, en la medida que a cada uno corresponda, dentro del ámbito de sus respectivas facultades, a llevar a cabo todos los actos convenientes y/o necesarios, incluyendo sin limitar, la firma de todos los documentos y/o la celebración de cualesquier contratos y/o convenios, en relación con lo anterior, en el entendido que la presente autorización, no constituye una dispensa a cualquier Eventos de Incumplimiento, ni la las consecuencias derivadas de los mismos.

QUINTO. By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 3 (Reuters) - The AI-fueled turbulence hitting markets in recent weeks has revived demand for many traditional safe-haven assets, with one glaring exception: gold.

Growing concerns about the stability and profitability of the AI boom have knocked the S&P 500 .SPX and Nasdaq .IXIC from record highs, pushing investors to seek protection in classic havens like US Treasuries US10YT=RR, the dollar .DXY, the Swiss franc CHF=, and the Japanese yen JPY=. But gold, the oldest safety play of all, has not found a bid.

The yellow metal XAU= slid below $4,000 an ounce on Friday, its lowest level in a year, despite a seemingly favorable "risk off" backdrop of falling stock prices, widening credit spreads, lower bond yields and diminishing expectations for US interest-rate hikes.

Even persistent weakness in bitcoin BTC=, once termed "digital gold", and last week's $6.3 billion cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance, potentially the world's biggest financial heist, have failed to offer gold any discernible support.

Nor has the eight-month US-Iran war. In fact, it has been a long time since gold displayed the safe-haven and inflation-hedge characteristics traditionally associated with it.

SAFETY TO SPECULATION

Central banks, among the world's most safety-conscious, conservative and price-insensitive investors, have ramped up gold purchases in recent years. That may reflect a desire to diversify away from the dollar amid volatile US policy decisions more than a firm belief in gold's safety appeal.

Figures from the World Gold Council on Tuesday show that central-bank purchases rose 42% in the third quarter to 321 metric tons, the highest quarterly total since the fourth quarter of 2024. Poland and China led officially reported buying.

But an International Monetary Fund paper in July found that bullion is not a "reliable" hedge against equity market volatility and perhaps never has been, despite the long-held belief otherwise, and that its safe-haven properties "are neither universal nor unconditional."

Not only is gold not functioning as a store of value, it often trades like a speculative asset. When gold hit a dizzying peak of $5,595 an ounce last January, one-week "realized" volatility shot up to 90%. That's meme-stock territory.

Right now, gold's correlation with equities is positive and strengthening. Suki Cooper and Steven Englander at Standard Chartered estimate that gold's positive correlation with the S&P 500 on a three-month rolling basis is up to 0.48, and on a one-month basis, to 0.69.

READY FOR A COMEBACK?

Gold has certainly had a wild two years. Having surged 65% last year, its best annual performance since the 1970s, some degree of rebalancing this year was always on the cards.

Gold has lost around a quarter of its value since the US and Israel first attacked Iran on February 28, as spiking energy prices and expectations of tighter monetary policy have diminished the allure of the non-yielding metal.

Bullion is now down 9% so far this year, making it the worst performer by year-to-date dollar returns in Bank of America's list of 14 major asset classes. That's notably worse than even government bonds, which only weeks ago offered the highest yields in a quarter of a century.

Is it time for a bounce? If you believe in mean reversion, then yes. Gold is the most oversold asset class in BofA's ranking, trading some 10% below its 200-day moving average in dollar terms. That's around five times more oversold than government bonds, by this metric, and it puts gold in the ballpark of markets like Chinese and Brazilian equities that have grabbed headlines recently for all the wrong reasons.

But what would spark a rebound? Probably not further stock market turbulence. If equity-market losses trigger liquidity needs, investors are more likely to sell gold than buy.

"In the short term, gold’s role as a liquidity provider and the need to generate cash are likely to overshadow its role as a safe-haven asset," Englander and Cooper wrote on Friday.

That's probably true. Perhaps it’s also time to ask whether gold may no longer be a reliable port in the storm.

(The opinions expressed here are those of Jamie McGeever, a columnist for Reuters)

The Mexican economy is expected to grow more, according to the October Survey of Private Sector Economic Specialists' Expectations by Banco de México. The growth forecast for 2026 increased from 1.40% in September to 1.61% in October. For 2027, the average forecast for GDP rose from 1.77% to 1.86%, according to the central bank.

Increased Optimism

According to the survey, there is also increased optimism about the economic situation. Those who believe the country's economy is better than it was a year ago rose from 46% in September to 64% in October. Meanwhile, the percentage of specialists who believe the business climate will improve in the coming months increased from 39% to 44%, and those who think it is a bad time to invest decreased from 46% to 39%. However, there are factors that could hinder economic growth. While governance remains the area with the highest percentage of responses at 38%, external conditions sharply rose as a risk factor, representing 21% in September and increasing to 33% in October. Individually, the most significant obstacles cited were foreign trade policy, public security issues, lack of structural change, and international political instability. The survey conducted among 40 analysis groups indicates that analysts have revised the peso-dollar exchange rate upward, with an average adjustment from 17.57 pesos to 18.25 pesos for the end of 2026. For 2027, the adjustment rose from 18.11 pesos to 18.58 pesos per dollar. Projections for overall inflation at year-end remained stable, with an average expectation of 3.85% to 3.83% for 2026, and also from 3.85% to 3.83% for the end of 2027.

November 3 (Axis negocios) -- The remittances sent to Mexico by workers abroad returned to a growth trend in September, as the year heads toward a flat advance amid an economy facing challenges.

During September 2026, the country received $5,362.2 million in remittances, marking an increase of 1.55% compared to the same month last year, according to a statement from Banco de México.

The increase represented both a sequential and annual rebound, as it followed August, which was the worst month of the year (-3.56%), and also marked the first time there was an increase in September after two consecutive months of decline.

The figure was "the net result of a 6.3% contraction in the number of transfers and an 8.4% increase in the average remittance amount," the monetary regulator stated in the release.

The average amount continued to sustain the indicator in September, rising for the thirteenth consecutive time and at its fastest pace in 57 months. However, the number of transactions fell for the 17th time in the last 18 months.

Remittances have been driven by the U.S. economy, its main source, which showed its best performance in four quarters during the third quarter of the year, according to preliminary readings.

Within that context, employment in the U.S. recorded two months of growth in September, although signs of deceleration remain. However, the situation for the Latino population is more uncertain due to U.S. policies targeting migrants and residents from that group.

The money that flowed into the country aligned with analysts' expectations, which anticipated $5,375 million with a 1.8% advance, according to Banorte Casa de Bolsa.

"Remittances rebounded in the year-on-year comparison in September," wrote Banorte specialists led by Juan Carlos Alderete in a report. "Positive results in September were aided by improved labor market conditions in the United States."

Analysts noted that the unemployment rate for Hispanic and Latino populations in the U.S. decreased in September, with a similar trend observed in the specific measure for Mexican migrants.

With the result for September, the total money that entered Mexico during the third quarter totaled $16,385.1 million, a 0.3% increase compared to the same period last year.

In this way, the indicator linked its two weakest third-quarter growths in the last 14 years.

In Mexican pesos, the currency used for spending in the country, Mexico received 92,605 million pesos, representing a decrease of 5.1% compared to the amount captured in September of the previous year, with an average exchange rate of 17.27 units per dollar, which strengthened by 7.1% during the period.

The inflow of remittances to the country reached 16 consecutive declines in local currency last month.

These resources represent one of the factors supporting domestic consumption, which was expected to decline for the first time in the last three months in September, according to the leading indicator from the National Statistics and Geography Institute.

For the nine months of the year so far, the indicator totaled $47,164 million, a figure that is 2.12% higher than that recorded in the same period last year, marking the 12th growth in 13 years.

"Our focus for the fourth quarter of 2026 will be on the dynamics of the agricultural and construction sectors in the United States," the Banorte specialists added. "In both, anti-migrant policies — particularly raids and deportations — have restricted the labor supply, including their effect on absenteeism levels."

* César Pérez contributed to this story

The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) for the manufacturing sector in Mexico fell from 50.3 in September to 49.5 in October, returning to contraction territory, according to data from S&P Global.

This result was attributed to a significant decline in industrial production, marking its largest drop in the last six months and extending the slowdown that began in July 2024.

"Mexican manufacturers experienced a weakening in the growth of new orders and an increase in cost pressures in October," said Pollyanna de Lima, Associate Economic Director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, in a statement. "Companies also faced challenges from rising costs and a hesitant increase in their own selling prices."

New orders received increased for the sixth consecutive month, although the growth rate was marginal and the weakest of the period. Some manufacturers noted resilience in demand, while others pointed to competition, the energy crisis, and diminishing customer interest in their products as significant challenges for the sector this month.

The stock exchanges in Mexico closed with moderate gains on Tuesday. The local indices trimmed the solid advances seen at the opening during a session marked by the midterm elections in the United States and labor figures.

The main index, S&P/BMV IPC, of the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV), which comprises the most traded local shares, rose by 0.52% to 70,143.09 points. The FTSE BIVA index, of the Institutional Stock Exchange (Biva), increased by 0.57% to 1,421.79 units.

Within the benchmark index, most stocks closed with gains. Notably, the airline Volaris saw an increase of 8.54% to 12.96 pesos, followed by Televisa, which rose 6.03% to 8.27 pesos, and Megacable, which gained 3.66% to 57.8 pesos.

The local stock market had surged more than 2% in the morning following a long weekend due to the Day of the Dead holiday in Mexico. Investors absorbed news and a decline in oil prices that brought the indices closer to historical highs.

Later, caution regarding the midterm legislative elections in the United States and strong labor figures in that country dampened investors' risk appetite. Following an 8.7% gain in October, the S&P/BMV IPC has risen nearly 9% year-to-date.

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. PHOENIX, Tuesday, Nov 03, 2026 - Southern Copper Corporation's (NYSE:SCCO $173.68) stock price traded at its 97-day low of $171.53. The last time the price hit that low level was on Wednesday, Jul 29, 2026.

Southern Copper Corporation's stock price fell $3.73 (2.1%) from its previous trading session to close at $173.68.

Compared with the S&P 500 Index which rose 22.8 points (0.3%) in the day, the relative price change was -2.4%.

SECTION 1 RECENT NEWS AND RESEARCH

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

SECTION 2 COMPANY DESCRIPTION

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Oct 21, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE and BVL: SCCO)

Exhibit 99.1

Victor Pedraglio

Bertin Galarreta

Adjusted EBITDA in 9M26 was $8,609.0 million, 56.2% higher than in 9M25. The adjusted EBITDA margin in 9M26 stood at 65.0% versus 57.7% in 9M25.

On a YTD basis, copper production fell 2.9% in 2026 to stand at 693,602 tonnes. This evolution was mainly driven by a decrease in production at our Peruvian mines due to lower ore grades. YoY the Company smelting and refining facilities increased their production by 15.8% and 10.1%, respectively.

On a YTD basis, mined silver production rose 1.5% compared to 2025. Zinc and molybdenum production were down 7.2% and 5.2% in 2026, respectively.

In 9M26, the operating cash cost per pound of copper, net of by-product revenue credits, was $0.01. This represents a decrease of 98.1% compared to the $0.61 reported in 9M25. The 9M26 cash cost decrease was driven by an increase in by-product revenue credits (+53.6%).

In lieu of fractional shares, cash will be distributed to each shareholder who would otherwise have been entitled to receive a fractional share, based on a share price of $197.83, which is the average of the high and low share price on October 15, 2026.

Mr. German Larrea, Chairman of the Board, commenting on the Companys progress and current circumstances, said: "We are very pleased with our strong third-quarter performance, which delivered a record for net sales, adjusted EBITDA and net income. These achievements were thanks to our strategy and disciplined cost control at the operational level.

Our Tia Maria project is reaching half completion this month, and significant goals have been achieved on different construction fronts. As planned, we have finished pre-stripping works at the La Tapada deposit to uncover areas where mineral can be extracted when we begin operations. Simultaneously, work in the dry and wet areas, where most of the solvent extraction and electrowinning activities will be performed, is advancing steadily and according to projected timelines.

SOUTHERN COPPER CORPORATION PRICES $1,250,000,000 UNSECURED NOTES DUE 2036

Phoenix, June 17, 2026 - Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE and LSE: SCCO) (the "Company") announces that on June 16, 2026, it priced US$1,250,000,000 principal amount of

5.350% Notes due 2036 (the Notes) in an underwritten, registered public offering. The transaction is expected to close on or about June 24, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. These notes will be general unsecured obligations of the

Company and will rank equally with all of its existing and future unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

The net proceeds from this offering will be used by Southern Peru Copper Corporation, Sucursal del Peru, our

Peruvian branch (SPCC), for the development of the Tia Maria project, the financing of the capital expenditure program of SPCC, and/or for general corporate purposes of SPCC, including but not limited to working capital (and expenses due in the

short term).

BofA Securities, Inc. and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC acted as global coordinators and joint bookrunners for the offering and Barclays Capital Inc. and Santander US

Capital Markets LLC acted as joint bookrunners for the offering.

The offering is being made pursuant to an effective shelf registration statement, and only by means of a prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus, copies of

which may be obtained by contacting BofA Securities, Inc. at +1-800-294-1322, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC at +1-800-624-1808, Barclays Capital Inc. at +1-929-694-1057 or Santander US Capital Markets LLC at +1-855-403-3636. Alternatively, you may get

these documents for free by visiting EDGAR on the website of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") at http://www.sec.gov/. Before you invest in the notes, you should read the prospectus supplement, the accompanying prospectus in the

registration statement and the other documents the Company has filed with the SEC for more complete information about the Company and this offering.

Southern Copper Corporation is one of the largest integrated copper producers in the world and we believe we have the largest copper reserves of any listed company.

Piedras Negras, Coahuila - The regional and municipal Civil Protection coordinations from the Central-Desert, Carboniferous, and Northern areas were summoned by the company Ferromex to participate in a training course on hazardous materials handling, which will take place at the railway company's facilities located on the borders of Nava and Piedras Negras, reported Francisco Contreras Obregón, the regional Civil Protection coordinator for Coahuila.

He noted that this training is of great importance, as the region has railway lines used for transporting hazardous materials through various municipalities, emphasizing the training provided by Ferromex through specialists.

During the course, Ferromex's training tank car and the Transcaer system will be utilized, tools that allow for the training of firefighting and emergency response teams, Contreras Obregón explained.

He added that some personnel from the Manantiales and Northern regions have already taken this course, making this training also a means to update their knowledge.

Through the border of Piedras Negras, hazardous materials such as ammonium nitrate, liquefied gas, and fuels, among other high-risk substances, are both imported and exported, which necessitates that firefighting and Civil Protection units are prepared to handle emergencies related to accidents involving the transportation of these products.

Contreras Obregón indicated that schools, universities, and private companies can also participate in these courses to train their students or personnel responsible for managing emergencies within their facilities.

Mexico produced 257,480t of rice in 2025, 17.3% more than the 219,587t recorded in 2024, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER). Despite the increase, domestic production remains insufficient to meet national consumption, and the government set a 200,000t duty-free import quota for 2026 to complement supply.

Figures from the Agrifood and Fisheries Information Service (SIAP) show that the value of production rose 12.5%, from MX$1.30 billion to MX$1.46 billion (US$68.9 million to US$77.5 million) over the same period. SADER attributed part of the result to a larger planted area, which increased 28.4%, from 31,346 ha to 40,250 ha.

Of the 12 producing states, Nayarit led national production with 79,737t, followed by Campeche with 61,670t and Michoacán with 37,300t. Together, the three states produced 178,707t, or 69.4% of the national total.

Campeche recorded the largest growth. In 2025, its planted area rose 166.3% to 12,837 ha, while production increased 134.8%, from 26,263t to 61,670t. SADER attributed these results to Plan Campeche, a strategy by the federal and state governments to increase rice, milk and meat production, create jobs and strengthen food sovereignty through direct support to producers.

Under the plan, small-scale rice producers receive incentives from the Production for Wellbeing program, free fertilizers and certified seed delivered directly, without intermediaries. Producers also receive technical support from specialists trained by a scientific committee of experts from four national and state institutions. The plan includes the delivery of machinery to modernize farm work and reduce costs, as well as public purchases of rice coordinated by Alimentación para el Bienestar and other federal and state agencies.

Support for rice producers extends beyond Campeche. On Oct. 29, SADER began distributing incentives to rice and wheat producers under the Fair Trade program, which will benefit 1,342 rice farmers and 14,157 wheat farmers. Other actions for rice producers, particularly in Nayarit and Campeche, include links to the Production for Wellbeing and Fertilizers for Wellbeing programs, financing through the Harvesting Sovereignty Credit, certified seed and production and marketing incentives.

As of September 2026, SIAP data show rice production of 90,626t on 37,080 ha planted. Nayarit contributed 46,060t, Tamaulipas 16,198t, Campeche 11,630t, Tabasco 7,054t and Jalisco 4,886t, together accounting for 94.7% of the total.

Import Quota to Cover the Supply Gap

Rice ranks fourth among the most consumed basic grains in Mexico. It is used mainly as a side dish and in the production of flours, beverages and animal feed. Even with higher output, Mexico relies heavily on imports to meet this demand. In 2024, imported paddy and milled rice made up 84% of the available supply. Most imports came from the United States, although sources diversified in 2025.

To secure supply, the Ministry of Economy (SE) published a decree in the DOF establishing a 200,000t duty-free import quota for paddy rice, valid until Dec. 31, 2026. The quota applies to tariff code 1006.10.99, which covers rice types other than Morelos rice. Mexico maintains phytosanitary requirements for paddy rice imports from Brazil, the United States, Guyana and Uruguay.

The quota is allocated through a public tender managed by the General Directorate of Trade Facilitation and Foreign Trade (DGFCCE) under the Minimum Price modality. Individuals and companies established in Mexico can participate. Quota certificates are transferable and valid until Dec. 31, 2026. According to the SE, the quota seeks to diversify supply sources, create competitive conditions and support price stability without discouraging domestic production

Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais SA (Usiminas), headquartered in Brazil, is a prominent steel producer specializing in the manufacturing of flat steel products, iron ore mining, and logistics services. As a key player in the Brazilian steel industry, the company focuses on integrated operations that encompass mining raw materials, producing steel through modern blast furnaces and rolling mills, and supplying high-quality products to domestic and international markets. Usiminas' core activities emphasize efficiency and sustainability, supporting sectors such as automotive, construction, and infrastructure. In recent years, the company's fastest-growing segments have been its high-value added steel products, including coated and galvanized steels, driven by rising demand in the automotive industry and export markets. This growth is further bolstered by strategic investments in technological upgrades and environmental initiatives, positioning Usiminas to capitalize on global trends toward sustainable manufacturing and infrastructure development. It is Brazil's 7th largest Iron/Steel company by market capitalization.

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261103:nNRA2k.html_limpio: Amid many negative perspectives regarding Lula's fourth presidential term, one particular issue should worry all Brazilians, regardless of political preference: his support for Davi Alcolumbre for another two years as President of the Senate. It is important to recall that Alcolumbre has stalled all impeachment requests against Supreme Court ministers, particularly Alexandre de Moraes, who is deeply entangled with Daniel Vorcaro. As Guilherme Cunha Pereira, president of Gazeta do Povo , points out, anyone who wishes to see the Constitution upheld cannot condone this immoral shielding. The Senate needs a new president, one with the courage to do what must be done.

The midterm elections in the United States are shaping up to be a decisive moment for the country's internal politics and its relationship with Mexico. During a panel discussion featuring Talya Isca, an internationalist; Raúl Benítez Manaut, a researcher and academic at the Center for North American Studies at UNAM; and Israel López, an editor and columnist at El Heraldo de México, they debated the current context marked by an electorate evaluating the performance of recent years and the role of key political figures on the U.S. stage.

In the debate held on the program "Noticias de la Tarde con Lupita Juárez" on Heraldo Televisión, the analysts pointed out that social and economic discontent, coupled with issues such as migration and energy management, are factors that could sway the results in the House of Representatives and the Senate. The expectations surrounding voter behavior, particularly in states of high commercial relevance to Mexico, keep observers alert to potential changes in legislative dynamics.

Perspectives on the Electorate and the Latino Vote

The Latino vote has been identified as a potentially decisive element in this electoral round. Although it has historically shown volatility, experts indicate that dissatisfaction with extreme immigration policies could mobilize this sector towards the Democratic Party. However, caution is advised in interpreting polls because there are segments of the electorate that are not always represented in traditional surveys.

Related News

  • 2026 Elections in the U.S.: These Are the 14 States Where You Can Vote Without Showing ID
  • INE Approves Voting in Preventive Detention for 21 Entities in the 2026-2027 Elections

"I think it's quite likely that the Democrats will at least win in the House, and I believe that would be quite significant because we need to analyze what context we are in," said Talya Isca, internationalist.

"The Latino vote usually votes for convenience, meaning they look for who offers them jobs. They voted for Donald Trump in both instances when he was fighting for the vote because he was a millionaire speaking on behalf of businesses, saying, 'I will offer jobs,'" commented Raúl Benítez Manaut, researcher and academic at the Center for North American Studies at UNAM.

Impact on Bilateral Relations with Mexico

The relationship between Mexico and the United States faces constant challenges, regardless of electoral outcomes. Specialists emphasize that, beyond the ideological differences between the parties, there are structural issues such as the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), border security, and immigration management that will remain priorities. It is underscored that pressure on Mexico, especially regarding security and trade issues, could persist or intensify depending on the results in Congress.

"Whoever wins, the Democrats aren't exactly pro-Mexican. In labor and wage issues, they set many conditions on the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement," noted Raúl Benítez Manaut, researcher and academic at the Center for North American Studies at UNAM.

"If the Republicans lose one or both chambers, Trump will heavily focus on foreign policy, as that will be his margin of maneuver now. With Mexico, he will tighten the reins to try to salvage the situation for the next two years," pointed out Israel López, editor and columnist at El Heraldo de México.

The United States is holding its midterm elections on November 3, and it appears that Xavier Becerra may emerge victorious as the governor of California.

This victory would be historic as it would mark the first time a governor of California with Mexican heritage has been elected.

Xavier Becerra's story is one of a man who helped support his family by working with his father in construction and who became the first member of his family to attend college.

Who is Xavier Becerra?

Xavier Becerra is an American politician of Mexican descent. He was born in Sacramento, California, to parents from Jalisco and California.

His father, Manuel Becerra, was born in Sacramento but grew up in Tijuana, Baja California.

How old is Xavier Becerra?

Xavier Becerra is 68 years old, having been born on January 26, 1958.

Who is Xavier Becerra's wife?

Carolina Reyes is the wife of Xavier Becerra, and they have been married for 38 years.

Dr. Carolina Reyes is a physician specializing in high-risk pregnancies, educated at Harvard, and an activist against racism.

What is Xavier Becerra's zodiac sign?

Xavier Becerra's zodiac sign is Aquarius, as he was born on January 26.

How many children does Xavier Becerra have?

Xavier Becerra and Carolina Reyes have three daughters:

  1. Clarisa
  2. Olivia
  3. Natalia

What did Xavier Becerra study?

Xavier Becerra studied two majors, the first in Economics and the second in Law, both at Stanford University.

What has Xavier Becerra done for work?

Xavier Becerra worked in construction alongside his father and held positions in Congress, the California State Attorney General's Office, and the Biden administration.

As a legislator in the U.S. House of Representatives, he served for 12 consecutive terms until 2017.

In the Biden administration, he was appointed to lead the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services in 2021.

What are Xavier Becerra's proposals?

Some of Xavier Becerra's proposals focus on addressing the housing crisis:

  • Build 40,000 affordable housing units
  • Streamline construction processes and permits
  • Expand state programs to assist with down payments for working families and veterans
  • Limit the mass purchase of residential properties by investors
  • Declare a state of emergency in California due to housing shortages
  • Expand direct approvals for real estate projects

MEXICO CITY (apro) .- Even if the Democrats take control of the United States Congress away from Donald Trump, it does not guarantee relief for Mexico. On the contrary, the Republican could tighten his protectionist policies by 2027 and keep the future of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) uncertain, analysts have agreed.

Amid the midterm elections taking place this November 3 in the United States, the Laboratory for Analysis in Trade, Economics and Business (LACEN) of UNAM indicated that a Democratic victory in one or both chambers of Congress does not mean Trump would lose the tools he has used to apply commercial pressure to his partners, nor that he would be stopped.

According to the LACEN analysis, rather than moderating his economic policy, in 2027, as a domino effect, "he will strengthen his economic nationalism and commercial patriotism."

"Through his laws, Trump will defend the interest of his commercial security, favoring domestic supply within productive chains in strategic sectors to ensure the prosperity and national security of the United States and reduce vulnerability to external supplies," the analysis document states.

In fact, LACEN anticipates that if Democratic lawmakers attempt to curtail the Republican's policies, he could resort to various forms of presidential veto.

The analysis platform Integralia also agrees that a Democratic victory would not necessarily represent a better scenario for the country. Even more so, the more obstacles Trump encounters within the United States, the greater his interest may be in focusing on foreign policy.

The midterm elections will modify the checks on Trump but will not necessarily reduce pressures on Mexico. A Democratic majority in one or both chambers would increase investigations and oversight of the Executive, intensifying internal political confrontation," it predicts.

Indeed, the Republican could seek a path through foreign policy to build his presidential legacy, and in that scenario, Mexico would again find itself at the center of U.S. demands.

As a result, "the fight against drug trafficking and organized crime, which enjoys greater bipartisan consensus than other international issues, could take on greater prominence and translate into new demands on Mexico. On the other hand, Republican losses in states affected by tariffs could increase pressures to moderate some trade measures."

The USMCA Remains in Limbo

For Integralia, regardless of whether the Democrats win or lose the U.S. Congress, USMCA negotiations will continue under the uncertainty that arose last July when the United States rejected extending the trade agreement for another 16 years.

"The USMCA will remain in effect, but uncertainty about its conditions will linger. The refusal of the United States to extend its validity for another 16 years in July 2026 opened a period of annual reviews. While the treaty remains in effect under the current provisions, disagreements persist over rules of origin, extraregional inputs, and China's participation in supply chains. Negotiations will follow their own dynamic, regardless of the election outcomes," it asserts.

Among the pending issues are the rules of origin, which determine what percentage of a product must be manufactured within North America to receive the benefits of the treaty; the use of inputs from countries outside the region; and, particularly, China's involvement in supply chains.

The Laws Trump Could Use to Apply Pressure

According to LACEN, the U.S. president has various legal tools that he could use to protect his industry and restrict the entry of foreign goods, even if the Democrats take control of Congress.

One of these tools is the Buy American Act, enacted in 1933 and also related to 2010 in the LACEN analysis, which allows for the prioritization of purchasing products made in the United States over foreign goods for certain federal acquisitions.

Another tool mentioned by LACEN is the National Security Act of 1947. However, this law does not by itself establish a general authority to impose tariffs, but rather is part of the legal framework for U.S. security and defense.

Regarding trade restrictions, one relevant provision is Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, which allows the president to adjust the imports of certain products when an investigation determines that their entry into the country threatens to harm U.S. national security.

New Nanoparticles Study Findings Have Been Reported by Investigators at Northwest University (N Modified Uniform Fe0 Nanoparticles Within Cnt for Efficient Removal of Methylene Blue From Wastewater)

2026 NOV 03-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Nanotech Daily-- A new study on Nanotechnology- Nanoparticles is now available. According to news originating from Shaanxi, People' s Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated," Fe and N co-loaded carbon nanotubes were synthesized through a coordination-assisted strategy for methylene blue... 2026 NOV 03 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Nanotech Daily -- A new study on Nanotechnology - Nanoparticles is now available. According to news originating from Shaanxi, People's Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated, "Fe and N co-loaded carbon nanotubes were synthesized through a coordination-assisted strategy for methylene blue MB removal. Structural characterization confirmed that Fe-N modification increased the defect density of CNT, improved pore accessibility, and promoted the dispersion of iron species."

Financial supporters for this research include National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), State Key Laboratory of Clean and Efficient Coal Utilization, Taiyuan University of Technology.

Our news journalists obtained a quote from the research from Northwest University, "The ID/IG value increased from 1.08 for CNT to 1.10 for Fe-N/CNT, while the specific surface area of Fe-N/CNT reached 209.7 m2 g- 1. Under the optimized conditions, MB concentration of 100 mg L- 1, adsorbent dosage of 25 mg, and contact time of 120 min, Fe-N/CNT exhibited an adsorption capacity of 108.98 mg g-1. This value was much higher than those of pristine CNT (60.67 mg g-1) and Fe/CNT (41.43 mg g- 1). The adsorption behavior fitted well with the pseudo-secondorder kinetic model (R2 = 0.9998) and the Langmuir isotherm model (R2 = 0.9977). Mechanism analysis suggested that electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, it-it stacking, pore filling, and Fe-Nx sites jointly contributed to MB adsorption. Fe-N/CNT retained 81% of its adsorption efficiency after five cycles and showed stable performance in cation-containing solutions, multi-dye systems, and fixed-bed column operation."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "These results demonstrate that Fe-N/CNT is a promising adsorbent for practical dye wastewater treatment."

This research has been peer-reviewed.

For more information on this research see: N Modified Uniform Fe0 Nanoparticles Within Cnt for Efficient Removal of Methylene Blue From Wastewater. Materials Chemistry and Physics , 2026;367. Materials Chemistry and Physics can be contacted at: Elsevier Science Sa, PO Box 564, 1001 Lausanne, Switzerland. (Elsevier - www.elsevier.com ; Materials Chemistry and Physics - http://www.journals.elsevier.com/materials-chemistry-and-physics/ )

The news correspondents report that additional information may be obtained from Shuang Li, Northwest University, School of Chemical Engineering, Xian 710069, Shaanxi, People's Republic of China. Additional authors for this research include He Qu, Xuedong Ma, Dongzheng Wang, Quanyu Shi, Like Fu and Hongfei Xiao.

The direct object identifier (DOI) for that additional information is: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matchemphys.2026.132966 . This DOI is a link to an online electronic document that is either free or for purchase, and can be your direct source for a journal article and its citation.

NEW YORK, Nov 3 (Reuters) - US crude oil and distillate stocks eased, while gasoline inventories rose in the latest week, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Crude stocks fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended October 30, the sources said on the condition of anonymity.

Gasoline stocks rose by 1.43 million barrels, while distillate inventories fell by 1.19 million barrels compared with a week earlier, the sources said.

(Reporting by Siddharth Cavale in New York; Editing by Franklin Paul)

(( siddharth.cavale@thomsonreuters.com ))

Argentine Ambassador Sebastian Sayus has offered Argentina's expertise in advanced agricultural machinery, grain storage technologies and post-harvest management to help Pakistan tackle significant losses in its agricultural produce, while identifying promising opportunities for joint ventures and business-to-business partnerships in... Argentine Ambassador Sebastian Sayus has offered Argentina's expertise in advanced agricultural machinery, grain storage technologies and post-harvest management to help Pakistan tackle significant losses in its agricultural produce, while identifying promising opportunities for joint ventures and business-to-business partnerships in agriculture, dairy and pharmaceuticals.

Speaking during his visit to the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Sayus highlighted that Pakistan lost 10-20% of its grain production and 35-40% of its horticultural produce annually, largely due to inefficient storage facilities and inadequate post-harvest management. He noted that Argentina, being one of the world's leading food-exporting countries, possessed considerable expertise in agricultural machinery and modern storage solutions, including silo bags and metallic silos, which could be effectively introduced and developed in Pakistan.

He expressed confidence that Argentina could play a meaningful role in helping Pakistan strengthen its agricultural supply chain, reduce wastage and improve the value of its agricultural output. With Pakistan increasingly focusing on large-scale agricultural storage solutions, he saw considerable scope for cooperation, technology transfer and mutually beneficial investment in this critical sector.

The ambassador also identified significant potential for collaboration in the dairy industry, besides highlighting Argentina's advanced pharmaceutical capabilities, especially in the manufacturing of oncology products used in cancer treatment.

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Recent News 2 of 3, Source: HourlyBusinessNews, 269 words

Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. DE C.V. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to acquire all or part of the shares and/or airport operators, including Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes, either directly or through its subsidiaries and/or special purpose vehicles. Resolutions thereon. II. Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.
