SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. Nov 02, 2026

Coca Cola FEMSA (NYSE:KOF - Get Free Report) had its price target boosted by Barclays from $122.00 to $125.00 in a research note issued on Tuesday, Benzinga reports. The brokerage presently has an "equal weight" rating on the stock. Barclays's price objective would indicate a potential upside of 6.59% from the stock's previous close.

Other equities research analysts also recently issued reports about the company. JPMorgan Chase & Co. raised their target price on Coca Cola FEMSA from $114.00 to $127.00 and gave the company a "neutral" rating in a report on Wednesday, July 15th. Weiss Ratings cut Coca Cola FEMSA from a "buy (b+)" rating to a "buy (b)" rating in a research note on Thursday. Wall Street Zen cut Coca Cola FEMSA from a "strong-buy" rating to a "buy" rating in a research note on Saturday, September 12th. The Goldman Sachs Group reiterated a "buy" rating and set a $129.00 price objective on shares of Coca Cola FEMSA in a research report on Wednesday, October 28th. Finally, HSBC lowered Coca Cola FEMSA from a "buy" rating to a "hold" rating and dropped their price target for the company from $120.00 to $116.00 in a research report on Tuesday, July 28th. Four research analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating and six have assigned a Hold rating to the company's stock. According to data from MarketBeat, the company currently has a consensus rating of "Hold" and a consensus target price of $121.43.

Get Our Latest Report on Coca Cola FEMSA

Coca Cola FEMSA Stock Performance

NYSE:KOF opened at $117.27 on Tuesday. Coca Cola FEMSA has a fifty-two week low of $85.35 and a fifty-two week high of $122.14. The firm's 50 day moving average is $112.55 and its two-hundred day moving average is $107.09. The company has a market cap of $197.09 billion, a P/E ratio of 17.90, a P/E/G ratio of 1.56 and a beta of 0.54. The company has a quick ratio of 0.87, a current ratio of 1.14 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.45.

Coca Cola FEMSA (NYSE:KOF - Get Free Report) last issued its earnings results on Monday, October 26th. The company reported $1.72 earnings per share for the quarter, missing the consensus estimate of $1.89 by ($0.17). Coca Cola FEMSA had a return on equity of 15.76% and a net margin of 7.95%. The firm had revenue of $4.41 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts' expectations of $4.36 billion. Analysts expect that Coca Cola FEMSA will post 6.98 EPS for the current year.

Hedge Funds Weigh In On Coca Cola FEMSA

Several large investors have recently made changes to their positions in the business. Whipplewood Advisors LLC lifted its holdings in shares of Coca Cola FEMSA by 862.2% during the first quarter. Whipplewood Advisors LLC now owns 433 shares of the company's stock worth $42,000 after buying an additional 388 shares during the last quarter. KBC Group NV acquired a new stake in shares of Coca Cola FEMSA in the first quarter worth $69,000. Mirae Asset Global Investments Co. Ltd. bought a new position in Coca Cola FEMSA during the third quarter worth $85,000. Community Financial Services Group LLC bought a new position in Coca Cola FEMSA during the second quarter worth $92,000. Finally, EverSource Wealth Advisors LLC raised its stake in Coca Cola FEMSA by 8.0% during the 1st quarter. EverSource Wealth Advisors LLC now owns 1,371 shares of the company's stock valued at $134,000 after purchasing an additional 101 shares during the last quarter.

Coca Cola FEMSA Company Profile

(Get Free Report)

Coca-Cola FEMSA, SAB. de C.V. is the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler by sales volume. The company produces, markets, sells and distributes beverages under The Coca-Cola Company's brands, including Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta and Powerade, as well as bottled water, juices, dairy products, sports drinks, energy drinks and other beverage products.

The company serves consumers through a broad distribution network that includes traditional retail stores, supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants, food-service businesses and other commercial channels.

El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, que agrupa a las acciones más negociadas del mercado local, ganaba un 0.84% a 70,367.51 puntos poco después de la apertura.

Megacable , led by Enrique Yamuni, does not rule out modifying its mobile phone strategy to attract more users to Altán Redes as Televisa moves forward with its plans to acquire AT&T in Mexico.

During a call with analysts, Raymundo Fernández , an executive at Megacable, explained that the majority of its 845,000 mobile lines currently operate on Altán's infrastructure, while another portion uses AT&T's network.

The company could transfer more customers to Altán in 2027 and is even considering the possibility of migrating all its users to Altán Redes or establishing agreements with a third operator. For now, Megacable aims to maintain its commercial relationship with AT&T, although it acknowledges that the new scenario could lead to adjustments in the coming months.

Interestingly, Megacable also does not rule out taking advantage of sector consolidation for acquisitions and is exploring various options, from strengthening its fixed telecommunications business to repurchasing shares or increasing dividends, though it does not yet have a concrete operation to announce.

In the meantime, mobile telephony will remain a complementary business for Megacable, which does not plan to make significant investments in that segment. Its priority will be to leverage the fixed infrastructure it has built over the past years, as it defines the role that Altán Redes will play in its growth strategy.

Additionally, the company is making adjustments to its workforce. Megacable reduced more than 2,600 jobs compared to the close of 2025 and finished September with approximately 31,700 employees. This measure is part of a strategy to control costs and improve productivity, which also includes automation and artificial intelligence.

Discussion of the Federal Expenditure Budget Begins

The Chamber of Deputies is set to discuss this week the Federal Expenditure Budget for 2027 amid negotiations between agencies and institutions seeking increased resources.

The proposal includes spending exceeding 10 trillion pesos , of which around one trillion would be allocated to social programs. Legislators have until November 15 to approve it, although negotiations are anticipated to modify the distribution of resources.

One notable point is the budget for the National Electoral Institute (INE) , which has been allocated 42,274.5 million pesos in a year when it will have to organize one of the largest electoral processes in its history.

It remains to be seen whether the resignation of Guadalupe Taddei Zavala from the presidency of the organization will have any impact on negotiations, especially after previous processes where legislators did not authorize the full amount requested by the INE.

For now, days of negotiations are expected in San Lázaro , although it is unclear how much the deputies will alter the Treasury's proposal.

OECD Holds Meeting with the SHCP

The week began actively in the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP) , following a meeting yesterday between Aida Caldera, head of the National Studies Division at the OECD , and María del Carmen Bonilla, Undersecretary of Finance .

The meeting focused on two topics of interest for the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development : understanding the federal government's plans for sustainable financing in a more challenging environment due to high international interest rates, and assessing public debt indicators.

Caldera highlighted that Mexico offers valuable insights for other emerging economies, thanks to its efforts to incorporate sustainability criteria into public finances and debt management, through the issuance of sovereign bonds aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

For her part, Bonilla explained that Mexico has been working with multilateral organizations such as the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and the World Bank to secure financing for projects of the current administration, including the Mexico Plan.

The undersecretary assured that the federal budget is fully aligned with the SDGs, contributing to the development of a sustainable debt market. Since 2020, the issuance of thematic instruments in the Mexican market has exceeded 91 billion dollars.

This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Industrias Penoles SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican mining company, focuses on the exploration, extraction, and processing of metallic minerals. Its core business activities include the production of essential metals such as zinc, lead, silver, and gold, alongside the manufacture of chemical products through subsidiaries like Penoles Chemicals. Operating primarily in Mexico, the company leverages advanced technologies to ensure efficient resource management and supply chain operations. Among its fastest-growing segments are silver mining and precious metals processing, fueled by rising global demand in electronics, renewable energy, and industrial applications. Penoles maintains a strong commitment to sustainability, emphasizing environmental responsibility and innovation to support long-term growth and operational excellence. It is Mexico's 2nd largest Mining company by market capitalization.

Promotora Y Operadora De Infraestructura, S.A.B. De C.V. (PINFRA), a leading Mexican infrastructure company listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, specializes in the development, construction, operation, and maintenance of transportation and infrastructure assets. Its core activities encompass toll roads, bridges, airports, and railways, primarily through public-private concessions that generate revenue via user fees and long-term contracts. The company plays a vital role in Mexico's economic growth by enhancing connectivity and mobility across key regions. Among its fastest-growing segments are airport operations, which have expanded significantly due to increasing passenger traffic and new terminal developments, as well as concessions for modern toll highways that benefit from rising vehicular demand and government infrastructure initiatives. PINFRA's strategic focus on sustainable projects and operational efficiency has positioned it as a key player in the sector, contributing to national development while delivering consistent returns for shareholders. It is Mexico's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Moises Ruben Kolteniuk Toyber

Director

Mr. Moises Ruben Kolteniuk Toyber serves as Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. In the past, he worked in the mining sector, within the Federal Government, as well as he has been Advisor of the mining area. Additionally, he served as Member of the Board of Directors of Aeropuertos del Sureste. He holds a degree in Electromechanical Engineering from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico and a Masters degree in Operations Research from the University of California at Berkeley.

Adriana Graciela Penaloza Alanis

Director

She holds a Bachelors degree in Graphics Design from Universidad Iberoamericana and a Masters degree in History of Art from Universidad Anahuac.

Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez

Independent Director

Mr. Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He is Chairman of the Company's Audit Committee and Member of the Corporate Practices Committee. He is also Associate Partner of the firm Solloa, Tello de Meneses y Compania SC. In addition, he has been Commissioner and Member of the Board of Directors of various companies within the industrial, commercial and financial sectors. He holds a degree in Public Accounting from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, a diploma in Financial Engineering from Colegio de Contadores Publicos de Mexico and a diploma in High Management from Universidad Iberoamericana.

Luis Hoyo Garcia

Independent Director

Mr. Luis Hoyo Garcia serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He is Member of the Company's Audit Committee and Chairman of the Corporate Practices Committee. He has also been Chief Executive Officer of Agencia Aduanal Luis Hoyo and Chairman of Association of Duty Agents in Lazaro Cardenas, Michoacan. He graduated in Public Accounting from Universidad Anahuac.

Frantz Joseph Guns Devos

Independent Director

Mr. Frantz Joseph Guns Devos serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He has worked at Aeropuertos del Sureste, Infraestructura Portuaria Mexicana and Ferrocarriles del Sureste. He has also been Consultant in the areas of project management, strategic planning and corporate government. He holds a Bachelors degree in Applied Economics from Universitaire Faculteiten Sint-Ignatius Antwerp (UFSIA).

Megacable will maintain its business relationship with AT&T Mexico, even with the acquisition of this company by Grupo Televisa, one of its main competitors in fixed networks. However, Megacable indicated that it could transfer all mobile customers currently served through AT&T to Altán Redes, without altering its business strategy.

The company, which currently has 844,841 mobile subscribers, believes that this business will continue as a complement to its Internet and pay-TV services, without the need for additional investment in cellular infrastructure, company executives stated during a conference call with analysts regarding the third-quarter results of 2026.

"We would like to maintain the relationship with AT&T if they wish to continue, but we have no issue moving all our subscribers to the Altán platform if needed," said Raymundo Fernández, Deputy General Director of Megacable.

Currently, the majority of Megacable's mobile users receive service through the infrastructure of Altán Redes, operator of the Shared Network, while a minority utilizes the AT&T Mexico network.

The acquisition of AT&T by Televisa introduces a new variable in that wholesale relationship, as Megacable and Izzi, a subsidiary of Televisa, compete directly for broadband and pay-TV customers in various cities across the country.

However, the acquisition still must complete its closing process, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027. Megacable executives did not announce the termination of their agreement with AT&T nor anticipatory decisions from Televisa regarding the continuation of the wholesale service.

Telcel was already in Megacable's plans

The possibility of diversifying mobile providers did not arise with the announcement of AT&T's acquisition.

El Economista reported on May 8 that Megacable was seeking a strategic alliance with Telcel, operator of América Móvil, to enhance its mobile offering and complement the services it already received from AT&T and Altán Redes.

"In mobile, we have the best service from two companies. One is AT&T, and the other is Altán. We are looking at how to integrate more players, like Telcel, in the future," Fernández told El Economista at that time.

The intention was to leverage Telcel's coverage to expand Megacable's commercial possibilities and offer mobile connectivity in more areas of the country, particularly where the infrastructure of its current providers showed limitations.

At that time, Megacable had 740,354 mobile subscribers.

The reported base now stands at 844,841 users, a difference of 104,487 lines, equivalent to a 14.1% growth compared to the figure released in May.

The fixed business will continue to concentrate investments

Fernández insisted that Megacable does not intend to divert resources from its primary activity to build a mobile operation with its own infrastructure.

"Mobile service is a complement for our subscribers; it does not require Capex, goes directly to our network, and contributes to the company," he explained.

"We are focusing on what we told you before and we are not wasting any strategic effort of our company on convergence issues," the executive added.

This stance confirms that mobile telephony will continue to function as a commercial tool to strengthen relationships with customers of fixed services, rather than becoming a new capital-intensive activity.

This position aligns with Megacable's shift in financial priorities after five years of infrastructure expansion.

At the close of the third quarter of 2026, the company reported 19.91 million homes covered and 6.08 million Internet subscribers, while its network reached a length of 111,855 kilometers.

lseg:urn:newsml:reuters.com:20261102:nNR.html_limpio:
Shayne O'Brien loves Topo Chico so much that when he heard that the cult favorite sparkling water might be disappearing from shelves, he rushed to stockpile more than 200 bottles.

Even that wouldn't be enough to get him through the great Topo Chico drought of 2026. O'Brien, a cattle rancher and pastor outside Austin, notes that he is the author of a book on grief. And yet he said he wasn't fully prepared for what it would be like to be without his beloved beverage.

Parent company Coca-Cola issued a statement to CNN in February that it had stopped production pending necessary "upgrades" at its water source and bottling facility in Monterrey, Mexico.

That disruption ended up being so prolonged that executives cited it in an earnings call last week in response to analyst questions about slow sales across Coke products in North America.

"If you were to factor in the Topo Chico situation we've had this year, and you factor in the timing of investments — you take those out, our price mix for the year is pretty much within the band that we would look to deliver," said John Murphy, Coca-Cola's president and chief financial officer.

But executives confirmed that the restocking of Topo Chico was finally underway — starting in Texas, where it enjoys a particularly devoted following. The drink is known for its heavy carbonation and slightly salty flavor.

"We know people have missed Topo Chico, and we're excited to bring its iconic bubbles back to shelves, with plans to expand to additional U.S. markets in 2027," a company spokesperson said.

The shortage impacted only the brand's glass-bottle products. Topo Chico also makes canned carbonated water and alcoholic seltzers.

O'Brien, who doesn't drink alcohol, calls Topo Chico "pastor beer" and served it at a party celebrating the 21st birthday of his 1,200-person church. He said it captures the burn of soda for him but without the sugar.

He was thrilled to find the bottles back in stock locally. He'll be "fully restored," he said, when he can get his hands on the twist-of-lime version.

Topo Chico, a brand in Mexico since 1895, was first commercially distributed in the United States in the 1980s. Executives for the drink have credited Mexican expatriates for bringing it across the border. It especially took hold in Texas, where it was adopted as an indispensable ingredient in "ranch water," a tequila-and-lime drink.

With its acquisition by Coca-Cola in 2017 and a boom in Americans drinking seltzer water, the brand's recognition has since spread beyond the Lone Star State.

"The NYT discovers Topo Chico. It's all over," tweeted Bloomberg journalist Joe Weisenthal, a graduate of the University of Texas at Austin, after the New York Times published a 2016 story about the bubbly glass bottles.

In earnings released last week, Coca-Cola revenue in North America was flat in the third quarter of 2026, marking lackluster demand in the United States and Canada.

Instead, the company's sales were largely driven by success in Latin America and Asia. Sales for Coke Zero exploded, growing by 16 percent worldwide. Diet Coke, sometimes nicknamed a "fridge cigarette," performed less well, increasing in sales by only 6 percent.

This isn't the first time that Topo Chico has suffered from shortages. During the pandemic, a crunch in raw materials prompted Texas grocery stores to limit how many bottles people could purchase at a time, according to local news outlets.

Trey Melcher, owner of a bar called Railyard in Houston, recalled trying out alternatives like San Pellegrino, Perrier and another Mexican sparkling water called Hethe. But customers weren't as enthusiastic.

With Topo Chico, "if you open a bottle, it stays carbonated much longer than some of the other options out there," he said. "Really, nothing seems to do as well as just regular Topo Chico in a glass bottle for us."

Megacable, un operador de telecomunicaciones mexicano, mantendrá su estrategia de maximizar el valor de su negocio, centrada principalmente en servicios de línea fija, tras la adquisición del negocio móvil de AT&T en México por parte de su competidor Grupo Televisa. La empresa continuará ofreciendo servicios como operador móvil virtual y no anticipa inversiones relacionadas con la adquisición de Televisa, el segundo operador móvil más grande del país. Megacable cuenta actualmente con 844,841 suscriptores a su servicio móvil, que opera principalmente utilizando la infraestructura de Altán Redes, con una menor porción en la infraestructura de AT&T. Por otro lado, Mercado Libre, la plataforma de comercio electrónico latinoamericana, inauguró su primer centro logístico en Tezontepec, Hidalgo, que incorpora robots para la preparación y procesamiento de pedidos. Esta instalación, parte de una inversión acumulativa de $604 millones en Hidalgo, comenzará operaciones con 240 robots y se espera que alcance hasta 1,000 a plena capacidad. La expansión de Mercado Libre en Hidalgo forma parte de una inversión anunciada de más de $4.6 mil millones para México hasta 2026.

En el ámbito tecnológico, las acciones de Intel, fabricante estadounidense de chips y semiconductores, experimentaron su mayor caída diaria desde 1974 tras proyectar ingresos y ganancias por debajo de lo esperado para el cuarto trimestre, debido a la debilidad en el mercado de computadoras personales. Las acciones de Intel cayeron un 29%, marcando su peor rendimiento en más de cinco décadas, cerrando a $65.76, el nivel más bajo desde abril. La compañía espera ingresos entre $15 mil millones y $16 mil millones para el último trimestre, por debajo de los aproximadamente $17 mil millones anticipados por analistas.

Finalmente, Alaska Air Group anunció que recortará alrededor de 200 empleos no contractuales debido a los altos precios del combustible y desafíos geopolíticos que impactan sus finanzas, con su CEO advirtiendo sobre una posible pérdida anual de $700 millones. Estos recortes sugieren que la crisis de precios del combustible vinculada a la guerra con Irán está afectando el empleo en la industria aérea, mientras que Alaska Air enfrenta presión financiera creciente al buscar una expansión ambiciosa en los sectores de viajes internacionales y de primera clase.

La expansión de Mercado Libre en Hidalgo forma parte de una inversión anunciada de más de $4.6 mil millones para México hasta 2026.

En el ámbito tecnológico, las acciones de Intel, fabricante estadounidense de chips y semiconductores, experimentaron su mayor caída diaria desde 1974 tras proyectar ingresos y ganancias por debajo de lo esperado para el cuarto trimestre, debido a la debilidad en el mercado de computadoras personales. Las acciones de Intel cayeron un 29%, marcando su peor rendimiento en más de cinco décadas, cerrando a $65.76, el nivel más bajo desde abril. La compañía espera ingresos entre $15 mil millones y $16 mil millones para el último trimestre, por debajo de los aproximadamente $17 mil millones anticipados por analistas.

Finalmente, Alaska Air Group anunció que recortará alrededor de 200 empleos no contractuales debido a los altos precios del combustible y desafíos geopolíticos que impactan sus finanzas, con su CEO advirtiendo sobre una posible pérdida anual de $700 millones. Estos recortes sugieren que la crisis de precios del combustible vinculada a la guerra con Irán está afectando el empleo en la industria aérea, mientras que Alaska Air enfrenta presión financiera creciente al buscar una expansión ambiciosa en los sectores de viajes internacionales y de primera clase.

Arca Continental, one of the five largest Coca-Cola bottlers globally, increased its sales and operating cash flow (EBITDA) by 6% in the third quarter, surpassing analysts' expectations, driven by its performance in Latin America.

In Mexico, sales grew by 3.7% and EBITDA by 7.5%, while in South America, the increases were 30% and 23%, respectively, allowing the company to offset declines in the United States, where revenues decreased by 0.8% and operating income before depreciation and amortization fell by 3.3%.

On a consolidated basis, AC's sales volume rose by 4.6%, with the strongest growth occurring in the bulk water segment at 7.3%; non-carbonated beverages at 7.1%; and flavored sodas at 7%. Water was the only segment that registered a decline.

In Mexico, the company emphasized the improvement in its profitability, as the operating cash flow margin expanded by 80 basis points to 24.7%, establishing it as the highest among its operational regions.

"Returnable and personal formats increased in mix, serving as commercial levers within a price-pack architecture designed to enhance affordability and support business profitability," the company stated in its report.

In South America, sales volumes performed favorably, even in Argentina. Growth was 17.5% during the third quarter and 10.5% year-to-date.

La compañía continuará ofreciendo servicios como operador móvil virtual, por lo que no anticipó posibles inversiones ante la compra que hará de Televisa, el segundo mayor operador móvil del país, dijeron directivos durante una conferencia con analistas e inversionistas.

Megacable suma actualmente 844,841 suscriptores de su servicio móvil que opera en su mayoría bajo la infraestructura de Altán Redes, una empresa mexicana de telecomunicaciones encargada de diseñar, desplegar y operar la Red Compartida, otra parte minoritaria opera bajo la infraestructura de AT&T.

Mercado Libre, la plataforma latinoamericana de comercio electrónico fundada en Argentina, inauguró en el municipio de Tezontepec, Hidalgo, su primer centro logístico (fulfillment center) que incorpora robots destinados para la preparación y el procesamiento de pedidos.

La instalación, que forma parte de una inversión acumulada de 604 millones de dólares en Hidalgo, comenzará a operar con 240 robots y llegará a 1,000 cuando opere a su máxima capacidad.

La expansión de Mercado Libre en Hidalgo estaba contemplada en la inversión de más de 4,600 millones de dólares que la empresa anunció para México en 2026.

Las acciones de Intel, fabricante estadounidense de chips y semiconductores, registraron su mayor caída diaria desde 1974, luego de que la compañía anticipó ingresos y ganancias inferiores a las esperadas para el cuarto trimestre, ante la persistente debilidad del mercado de computadoras personales.

Intel perdió 29%, su peor desempeño bursátil en más de cinco décadas. Los títulos cerraron en 65.76 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde abril.

Intel prevé ingresos de entre 15,000 y 16,000 millones de dólares para el último trimestre del año, por debajo de los aproximadamente 17,000 millones que esperaban los analistas.

Alaska Air Group anunció que recortará unos 200 puestos de trabajo no contractuales, ya que el aumento vertiginoso de los precios del combustible y los desafíos geopolíticos están afectando sus finanzas, y su director ejecutivo advirtió sobre una posible pérdida anual de 700 millones de dólares.

Estos recortes sugieren que la crisis de los precios del combustible vinculada a la guerra con Irán —que ya ha llevado a las aerolíneas estadounidenses a aumentar las tarifas y frenar el crecimiento de los vuelos— ahora está afectando los empleos en la industria aérea.

También ponen de relieve la creciente presión financiera sobre Alaska Air, que persigue una ambiciosa expansión en el sector de los viajes internacionales y de primera clase, con un fuerte crecimiento de los ingresos que lucha por compensar el aumento de los costos del combustible.

In light of inflationary pressures and the potential for further adjustments to its products, Arca Continental, one of the leading bottlers of Coca-Cola, anticipates that price increases in Mexico will remain above inflation levels.

"We expect to continue having prices above inflation. Price setting is not just about the price itself, but also about strategy and how we will continue to leverage our tools and promotional strategy to maintain prices above inflation," said Juan Claude Tissot, the company's Chief Operating Officer.

During a conference with analysts reviewing third-quarter results, he added that the strategy of providing affordable returnable containers allows for addressing different price levels while contributing to the profitability of the business.

He also mentioned the push for premium pricing on certain presentations and brands.

In the third quarter of 2026, Arca Continental raised its prices by 3.5% in Mexico compared to the same period the previous year, reported Emilio Marcos Charur, the company's Chief Financial Officer.

He emphasized that the price increase, along with volume growth and a greater share of returnable containers and single-serve presentations in the product mix, contributed to the operations' performance in Mexico during the third quarter.

"We should also consider coverage strategies and the lower sugar prices during the quarter. We will continue working to maintain this positive trend and expect the year to close with the same trend as in the first nine months of 2026," added Emilio Marcos Charur.

In Mexico, Arca Continental's beverage volume grew by 2.1% during the third quarter compared to the same period last year, marking an improvement over previous periods.

Year-to-date, the growth was 0.7% compared to the same period in 2025.

EBITDA increased by 7.5%, with the margin expanding by 80 basis points to 24.7%, compared to the third quarter of 2025, while beverage volume in Mexico grew by 2.1 percent.

On a consolidated level, Arca Continental's net sales rose by 5.9% to 66.613 billion pesos, while EBITDA increased by 6.2% to 13.625 billion pesos.

However, net income fell by 4.8% to 5.054 billion pesos in the comparison period.

During the conference with analysts, Arturo Gutiérrez Hernández, the company's CEO, noted that it has been a good year for Arca Continental, due to the capacities it has developed, positioning it to seize future opportunities in its main categories as well as in new products.

He added that they are better equipped to face the tax increases in 2026 compared to 2014, when they went through a similar situation.

"We need to be able to operate in a more complex environment in the future. And that is what we have been preparing for in recent years in terms of investment in the supply chain, capabilities, human technology, etc.," emphasized Arturo Gutiérrez.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.
